1/* stb_image_resize2 - v2.14 - public domain image resizing
2
3 by Jeff Roberts (v2) and Jorge L Rodriguez
4 http://github.com/nothings/stb
5
6 Can be threaded with the extended API. SSE2, AVX, Neon and WASM SIMD support. Only
7 scaling and translation is supported, no rotations or shears.
8
9 COMPILING & LINKING
10 In one C/C++ file that #includes this file, do this:
11 #define STB_IMAGE_RESIZE_IMPLEMENTATION
12 before the #include. That will create the implementation in that file.
13
14 EASY API CALLS:
15 Easy API downsamples w/Mitchell filter, upsamples w/cubic interpolation, clamps to edge.
16
17 stbir_resize_uint8_srgb( input_pixels, input_w, input_h, input_stride_in_bytes,
18 output_pixels, output_w, output_h, output_stride_in_bytes,
19 pixel_layout_enum )
20
21 stbir_resize_uint8_linear( input_pixels, input_w, input_h, input_stride_in_bytes,
22 output_pixels, output_w, output_h, output_stride_in_bytes,
23 pixel_layout_enum )
24
25 stbir_resize_float_linear( input_pixels, input_w, input_h, input_stride_in_bytes,
26 output_pixels, output_w, output_h, output_stride_in_bytes,
27 pixel_layout_enum )
28
29 If you pass NULL or zero for the output_pixels, we will allocate the output buffer
30 for you and return it from the function (free with free() or STBIR_FREE).
31 As a special case, XX_stride_in_bytes of 0 means packed continuously in memory.
32
33 API LEVELS
34 There are three levels of API - easy-to-use, medium-complexity and extended-complexity.
35
36 See the "header file" section of the source for API documentation.

38 ADDITIONAL DOCUMENTATION
39
40 MEMORY ALLOCATION
41 By default, we use malloc and free for memory allocation. To override the
42 memory allocation, before the implementation #include, add a:
43
44 #define STBIR_MALLOC(size,user_data) ...
45 #define STBIR_FREE(ptr,user_data) ...
46
47 Each resize makes exactly one call to malloc/free (unless you use the
48 extended API where you can do one allocation for many resizes). Under
49 address sanitizer, we do separate allocations to find overread/writes.
50
51 PERFORMANCE
52 This library was written with an emphasis on performance. When testing
53 stb_image_resize with RGBA, the fastest mode is STBIR_4CHANNEL with
54 STBIR_TYPE_UINT8 pixels and CLAMPed edges (which is what many other resize
55 libs do by default). Also, make sure SIMD is turned on of course (default
56 for 64-bit targets). Avoid WRAP edge mode if you want the fastest speed.
57
58 This library also comes with profiling built-in. If you define STBIR_PROFILE,
59 you can use the advanced API and get low-level profiling information by
60 calling stbir_resize_extended_profile_info() or stbir_resize_split_profile_info()
61 after a resize.
62
63 SIMD
64 Most of the routines have optimized SSE2, AVX, NEON and WASM versions.
65
66 On Microsoft compilers, we automatically turn on SIMD for 64-bit x64 and
67 ARM; for 32-bit x86 and ARM, you select SIMD mode by defining STBIR_SSE2 or
68 STBIR_NEON. For AVX and AVX2, we auto-select it by detecting the /arch:AVX
69 or /arch:AVX2 switches. You can also always manually turn SSE2, AVX or AVX2
70 support on by defining STBIR_SSE2, STBIR_AVX or STBIR_AVX2.
71
72 On Linux, SSE2 and Neon is on by default for 64-bit x64 or ARM64. For 32-bit,
73 we select x86 SIMD mode by whether you have -msse2, -mavx or -mavx2 enabled
74 on the command line. For 32-bit ARM, you must pass -mfpu=neon-vfpv4 for both
75 clang and GCC, but GCC also requires an additional -mfp16-format=ieee to
76 automatically enable NEON.
77
78 On x86 platforms, you can also define STBIR_FP16C to turn on FP16C instructions
79 for converting back and forth to half-floats. This is autoselected when we
80 are using AVX2. Clang and GCC also require the -mf16c switch. ARM always uses
81 the built-in half float hardware NEON instructions.
82
83 You can also tell us to use multiply-add instructions with STBIR_USE_FMA.
84 Because x86 doesn't always have fma, we turn it off by default to maintain
85 determinism across all platforms. If you don't care about non-FMA determinism
86 and are willing to restrict yourself to more recent x86 CPUs (around the AVX
87 timeframe), then fma will give you around a 15% speedup.
88
89 You can force off SIMD in all cases by defining STBIR_NO_SIMD. You can turn
90 off AVX or AVX2 specifically with STBIR_NO_AVX or STBIR_NO_AVX2. AVX is 10%
91 to 40% faster, and AVX2 is generally another 12%.
92
93 ALPHA CHANNEL
94 Most of the resizing functions provide the ability to control how the alpha
95 channel of an image is processed.
96
97 When alpha represents transparency, it is important that when combining
98 colors with filtering, the pixels should not be treated equally; they
99 should use a weighted average based on their alpha values. For example,
100 if a pixel is 1% opaque bright green and another pixel is 99% opaque
101 black and you average them, the average will be 50% opaque, but the
102 unweighted average and will be a middling green color, while the weighted
103 average will be nearly black. This means the unweighted version introduced
104 green energy that didn't exist in the source image.
105
106 (If you want to know why this makes sense, you can work out the math for
107 the following: consider what happens if you alpha composite a source image
108 over a fixed color and then average the output, vs. if you average the
109 source image pixels and then composite that over the same fixed color.
110 Only the weighted average produces the same result as the ground truth
111 composite-then-average result.)
112
113 Therefore, it is in general best to "alpha weight" the pixels when applying
114 filters to them. This essentially means multiplying the colors by the alpha
115 values before combining them, and then dividing by the alpha value at the
116 end.
117
118 The computer graphics industry introduced a technique called "premultiplied
119 alpha" or "associated alpha" in which image colors are stored in image files
120 already multiplied by their alpha. This saves some math when compositing,
121 and also avoids the need to divide by the alpha at the end (which is quite
122 inefficient). However, while premultiplied alpha is common in the movie CGI
123 industry, it is not commonplace in other industries like videogames, and most
124 consumer file formats are generally expected to contain not-premultiplied
125 colors. For example, Photoshop saves PNG files "unpremultiplied", and web
126 browsers like Chrome and Firefox expect PNG images to be unpremultiplied.
127
128 Note that there are three possibilities that might describe your image
129 and resize expectation:
130
131 1. images are not premultiplied, alpha weighting is desired
132 2. images are not premultiplied, alpha weighting is not desired
133 3. images are premultiplied
134
135 Both case #2 and case #3 require the exact same math: no alpha weighting
136 should be applied or removed. Only case 1 requires extra math operations;
137 the other two cases can be handled identically.
138
139 stb_image_resize expects case #1 by default, applying alpha weighting to
140 images, expecting the input images to be unpremultiplied. This is what the
141 COLOR+ALPHA buffer types tell the resizer to do.
142
143 When you use the pixel layouts STBIR_RGBA, STBIR_BGRA, STBIR_ARGB,
144 STBIR_ABGR, STBIR_RX, or STBIR_XR you are telling us that the pixels are
145 non-premultiplied. In these cases, the resizer will alpha weight the colors
146 (effectively creating the premultiplied image), do the filtering, and then
147 convert back to non-premult on exit.
148
149 When you use the pixel layouts STBIR_RGBA_PM, STBIR_RGBA_PM, STBIR_RGBA_PM,
150 STBIR_RGBA_PM, STBIR_RX_PM or STBIR_XR_PM, you are telling that the pixels
151 ARE premultiplied. In this case, the resizer doesn't have to do the
152 premultipling - it can filter directly on the input. This about twice as
153 fast as the non-premultiplied case, so it's the right option if your data is
154 already setup correctly.
155
156 When you use the pixel layout STBIR_4CHANNEL or STBIR_2CHANNEL, you are
157 telling us that there is no channel that represents transparency; it may be
158 RGB and some unrelated fourth channel that has been stored in the alpha
159 channel, but it is actually not alpha. No special processing will be
160 performed.
161
162 The difference between the generic 4 or 2 channel layouts, and the
163 specialized _PM versions is with the _PM versions you are telling us that
164 the data *is* alpha, just don't premultiply it. That's important when
165 using SRGB pixel formats, we need to know where the alpha is, because
166 it is converted linearly (rather than with the SRGB converters).
167
168 Because alpha weighting produces the same effect as premultiplying, you
169 even have the option with non-premultiplied inputs to let the resizer
170 produce a premultiplied output. Because the intially computed alpha-weighted
171 output image is effectively premultiplied, this is actually more performant
172 than the normal path which un-premultiplies the output image as a final step.
173
174 Finally, when converting both in and out of non-premulitplied space (for
175 example, when using STBIR_RGBA), we go to somewhat heroic measures to
176 ensure that areas with zero alpha value pixels get something reasonable
177 in the RGB values. If you don't care about the RGB values of zero alpha
178 pixels, you can call the stbir_set_non_pm_alpha_speed_over_quality()
179 function - this runs a premultiplied resize about 25% faster. That said,
180 when you really care about speed, using premultiplied pixels for both in
181 and out (STBIR_RGBA_PM, etc) much faster than both of these premultiplied
182 options.
183
184 PIXEL LAYOUT CONVERSION
185 The resizer can convert from some pixel layouts to others. When using the
186 stbir_set_pixel_layouts(), you can, for example, specify STBIR_RGBA
187 on input, and STBIR_ARGB on output, and it will re-organize the channels
188 during the resize. Currently, you can only convert between two pixel
189 layouts with the same number of channels.
190
191 DETERMINISM
192 We commit to being deterministic (from x64 to ARM to scalar to SIMD, etc).
193 This requires compiling with fast-math off (using at least /fp:precise).
194 Also, you must turn off fp-contracting (which turns mult+adds into fmas)!
195 We attempt to do this with pragmas, but with Clang, you usually want to add
196 -ffp-contract=off to the command line as well.
197
198 For 32-bit x86, you must use SSE and SSE2 codegen for determinism. That is,
199 if the scalar x87 unit gets used at all, we immediately lose determinism.
200 On Microsoft Visual Studio 2008 and earlier, from what we can tell there is
201 no way to be deterministic in 32-bit x86 (some x87 always leaks in, even
202 with fp:strict). On 32-bit x86 GCC, determinism requires both -msse2 and
203 -fpmath=sse.
204
205 Note that we will not be deterministic with float data containing NaNs -
206 the NaNs will propagate differently on different SIMD and platforms.
207
208 If you turn on STBIR_USE_FMA, then we will be deterministic with other
209 fma targets, but we will differ from non-fma targets (this is unavoidable,
210 because a fma isn't simply an add with a mult - it also introduces a
211 rounding difference compared to non-fma instruction sequences.
212
213 FLOAT PIXEL FORMAT RANGE
214 Any range of values can be used for the non-alpha float data that you pass
215 in (0 to 1, -1 to 1, whatever). However, if you are inputting float values
216 but *outputting* bytes or shorts, you must use a range of 0 to 1 so that we
217 scale back properly. The alpha channel must also be 0 to 1 for any format
218 that does premultiplication prior to resizing.
219
220 Note also that with float output, using filters with negative lobes, the
221 output filtered values might go slightly out of range. You can define
222 STBIR_FLOAT_LOW_CLAMP and/or STBIR_FLOAT_HIGH_CLAMP to specify the range
223 to clamp to on output, if that's important.
224
225 MAX/MIN SCALE FACTORS
226 The input pixel resolutions are in integers, and we do the internal pointer
227 resolution in size_t sized integers. However, the scale ratio from input
228 resolution to output resolution is calculated in float form. This means
229 the effective possible scale ratio is limited to 24 bits (or 16 million
230 to 1). As you get close to the size of the float resolution (again, 16
231 million pixels wide or high), you might start seeing float inaccuracy
232 issues in general in the pipeline. If you have to do extreme resizes,
233 you can usually do this is multiple stages (using float intermediate
234 buffers).
235
236 FLIPPED IMAGES
237 Stride is just the delta from one scanline to the next. This means you can
238 use a negative stride to handle inverted images (point to the final
239 scanline and use a negative stride). You can invert the input or output,
240 using negative strides.
241
242 DEFAULT FILTERS
243 For functions which don't provide explicit control over what filters to
244 use, you can change the compile-time defaults with:
245
246 #define STBIR_DEFAULT_FILTER_UPSAMPLE STBIR_FILTER_something
247 #define STBIR_DEFAULT_FILTER_DOWNSAMPLE STBIR_FILTER_something
248
249 See stbir_filter in the header-file section for the list of filters.
250
251 NEW FILTERS
252 A number of 1D filter kernels are supplied. For a list of supported
253 filters, see the stbir_filter enum. You can install your own filters by
254 using the stbir_set_filter_callbacks function.
255
256 PROGRESS
257 For interactive use with slow resize operations, you can use the
258 scanline callbacks in the extended API. It would have to be a *very* large
259 image resample to need progress though - we're very fast.
260
261 CEIL and FLOOR
262 In scalar mode, the only functions we use from math.h are ceilf and floorf,
263 but if you have your own versions, you can define the STBIR_CEILF(v) and
264 STBIR_FLOORF(v) macros and we'll use them instead. In SIMD, we just use
265 our own versions.
266
267 ASSERT
268 Define STBIR_ASSERT(boolval) to override assert() and not use assert.h
269
270 PORTING FROM VERSION 1
271 The API has changed. You can continue to use the old version of stb_image_resize.h,
272 which is available in the "deprecated/" directory.
273
274 If you're using the old simple-to-use API, porting is straightforward.
275 (For more advanced APIs, read the documentation.)

408// Easy-to-use API:
409//
410// * stride is the offset between successive rows of image data
411// in memory, in bytes. specify 0 for packed continuously in memory
412// * colorspace is linear or sRGB as specified by function name
413// * Uses the default filters
414// * Uses edge mode clamped
415// * returned result is 1 for success or 0 in case of an error.

418// stbir_pixel_layout specifies:
419// number of channels
420// order of channels
421// whether color is premultiplied by alpha
422// for back compatibility, you can cast the old channel count to an stbir_pixel_layout
423typedef enum
424{
425 STBIR_1CHANNEL = 1,
426 STBIR_2CHANNEL = 2,
427 STBIR_RGB = 3, // 3-chan, with order specified (for channel flipping)
428 STBIR_BGR = 0, // 3-chan, with order specified (for channel flipping)
429 STBIR_4CHANNEL = 5,
430
431 STBIR_RGBA = 4, // alpha formats, where alpha is NOT premultiplied into color channels
432 STBIR_BGRA = 6,
433 STBIR_ARGB = 7,
434 STBIR_ABGR = 8,
435 STBIR_RA = 9,
436 STBIR_AR = 10,
437
438 STBIR_RGBA_PM = 11, // alpha formats, where alpha is premultiplied into color channels
439 STBIR_BGRA_PM = 12,
440 STBIR_ARGB_PM = 13,
441 STBIR_ABGR_PM = 14,
442 STBIR_RA_PM = 15,
443 STBIR_AR_PM = 16,
444
445 STBIR_RGBA_NO_AW = 11, // alpha formats, where NO alpha weighting is applied at all!
446 STBIR_BGRA_NO_AW = 12, // these are just synonyms for the _PM flags (which also do
447 STBIR_ARGB_NO_AW = 13, // no alpha weighting). These names just make it more clear
448 STBIR_ABGR_NO_AW = 14, // for some folks).
449 STBIR_RA_NO_AW = 15,
450 STBIR_AR_NO_AW = 16,
451
452} stbir_pixel_layout;

483typedef enum
484{
485 STBIR_EDGE_CLAMP = 0,
486 STBIR_EDGE_REFLECT = 1,
487 STBIR_EDGE_WRAP = 2, // this edge mode is slower and uses more memory

491typedef enum
492{
493 STBIR_FILTER_DEFAULT = 0, // use same filter type that easy-to-use API chooses
494 STBIR_FILTER_BOX = 1, // A trapezoid w/1-pixel wide ramps, same result as box for integer scale ratios
495 STBIR_FILTER_TRIANGLE = 2, // On upsampling, produces same results as bilinear texture filtering
496 STBIR_FILTER_CUBICBSPLINE = 3, // The cubic b-spline (aka Mitchell-Netrevalli with B=1,C=0), gaussian-esque
497 STBIR_FILTER_CATMULLROM = 4, // An interpolating cubic spline
498 STBIR_FILTER_MITCHELL = 5, // Mitchell-Netrevalli filter with B=1/3, C=1/3
499 STBIR_FILTER_POINT_SAMPLE = 6, // Simple point sampling
500 STBIR_FILTER_OTHER = 7, // User callback specified
501} stbir_filter;

522//===============================================================
523// Extended-complexity API
524//
525// This API exposes all resize functionality.
526//
527// * Separate filter types for each axis
528// * Separate edge modes for each axis
529// * Separate input and output data types
530// * Can specify regions with subpixel correctness
531// * Can specify alpha flags
532// * Can specify a memory callback
533// * Can specify a callback data type for pixel input and output
534// * Can be threaded for a single resize
535// * Can be used to resize many frames without recalculating the sampler info
536//
537// Use this API as follows:
538// 1) Call the stbir_resize_init function on a local STBIR_RESIZE structure
539// 2) Call any of the stbir_set functions
540// 3) Optionally call stbir_build_samplers() if you are going to resample multiple times
541// with the same input and output dimensions (like resizing video frames)
542// 4) Resample by calling stbir_resize_extended().
543// 5) Call stbir_free_samplers() if you called stbir_build_samplers()
544//--------------------------------
545
546
547// Types:
548
549// INPUT CALLBACK: this callback is used for input scanlines
550typedef void const * stbir_input_callback( void * optional_output, void const * input_ptr, int num_pixels, int x, int y, void * context );
551
552// OUTPUT CALLBACK: this callback is used for output scanlines
553typedef void stbir_output_callback( void const * output_ptr, int num_pixels, int y, void * context );
554
555// callbacks for user installed filters
556typedef float stbir__kernel_callback( float x, float scale, void * user_data ); // centered at zero
557typedef float stbir__support_callback( float scale, void * user_data );
558
559// internal structure with precomputed scaling
560typedef struct stbir__info stbir__info;
561
562typedef struct STBIR_RESIZE // use the stbir_resize_init and stbir_override functions to set these values for future compatibility
563{
564 void * user_data;
565 void const * input_pixels;
566 int input_w, input_h;
567 double input_s0, input_t0, input_s1, input_t1;
568 stbir_input_callback * input_cb;
569 void * output_pixels;
570 int output_w, output_h;
571 int output_subx, output_suby, output_subw, output_subh;
572 stbir_output_callback * output_cb;
573 int input_stride_in_bytes;
574 int output_stride_in_bytes;
575 int splits;
576 int fast_alpha;
577 int needs_rebuild;
578 int called_alloc;
579 stbir_pixel_layout input_pixel_layout_public;
580 stbir_pixel_layout output_pixel_layout_public;
581 stbir_datatype input_data_type;
582 stbir_datatype output_data_type;
583 stbir_filter horizontal_filter, vertical_filter;
584 stbir_edge horizontal_edge, vertical_edge;
585 stbir__kernel_callback * horizontal_filter_kernel; stbir__support_callback * horizontal_filter_support;
586 stbir__kernel_callback * vertical_filter_kernel; stbir__support_callback * vertical_filter_support;
587 stbir__info * samplers;
588} STBIR_RESIZE;
589
590// extended complexity api
591
592
593// First off, you must ALWAYS call stbir_resize_init on your resize structure before any of the other calls!
594STBIRDEF void stbir_resize_init( STBIR_RESIZE * resize,
595 const void *input_pixels, int input_w, int input_h, int input_stride_in_bytes, // stride can be zero
596 void *output_pixels, int output_w, int output_h, int output_stride_in_bytes, // stride can be zero
597 stbir_pixel_layout pixel_layout, stbir_datatype data_type );
598
599//===============================================================
600// You can update these parameters any time after resize_init and there is no cost
601//--------------------------------
602
603STBIRDEF void stbir_set_datatypes( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, stbir_datatype input_type, stbir_datatype output_type );
604STBIRDEF void stbir_set_pixel_callbacks( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, stbir_input_callback * input_cb, stbir_output_callback * output_cb ); // no callbacks by default
605STBIRDEF void stbir_set_user_data( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, void * user_data ); // pass back STBIR_RESIZE* by default
606STBIRDEF void stbir_set_buffer_ptrs( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, const void * input_pixels, int input_stride_in_bytes, void * output_pixels, int output_stride_in_bytes );
607
608//===============================================================
609
610
611//===============================================================
612// If you call any of these functions, you will trigger a sampler rebuild!
613//--------------------------------
614
615STBIRDEF int stbir_set_pixel_layouts( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, stbir_pixel_layout input_pixel_layout, stbir_pixel_layout output_pixel_layout ); // sets new buffer layouts
616STBIRDEF int stbir_set_edgemodes( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, stbir_edge horizontal_edge, stbir_edge vertical_edge ); // CLAMP by default
617
618STBIRDEF int stbir_set_filters( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, stbir_filter horizontal_filter, stbir_filter vertical_filter ); // STBIR_DEFAULT_FILTER_UPSAMPLE/DOWNSAMPLE by default
619STBIRDEF int stbir_set_filter_callbacks( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, stbir__kernel_callback * horizontal_filter, stbir__support_callback * horizontal_support, stbir__kernel_callback * vertical_filter, stbir__support_callback * vertical_support );
620
621STBIRDEF int stbir_set_pixel_subrect( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, int subx, int suby, int subw, int subh ); // sets both sub-regions (full regions by default)
622STBIRDEF int stbir_set_input_subrect( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, double s0, double t0, double s1, double t1 ); // sets input sub-region (full region by default)
623STBIRDEF int stbir_set_output_pixel_subrect( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, int subx, int suby, int subw, int subh ); // sets output sub-region (full region by default)
624
625// when inputting AND outputting non-premultiplied alpha pixels, we use a slower but higher quality technique
626// that fills the zero alpha pixel's RGB values with something plausible. If you don't care about areas of
627// zero alpha, you can call this function to get about a 25% speed improvement for STBIR_RGBA to STBIR_RGBA
628// types of resizes.
629STBIRDEF int stbir_set_non_pm_alpha_speed_over_quality( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, int non_pma_alpha_speed_over_quality );
630//===============================================================
631
632
633//===============================================================
634// You can call build_samplers to prebuild all the internal data we need to resample.
635// Then, if you call resize_extended many times with the same resize, you only pay the
636// cost once.
637// If you do call build_samplers, you MUST call free_samplers eventually.
638//--------------------------------
639
640// This builds the samplers and does one allocation
641STBIRDEF int stbir_build_samplers( STBIR_RESIZE * resize );
642
643// You MUST call this, if you call stbir_build_samplers or stbir_build_samplers_with_splits
644STBIRDEF void stbir_free_samplers( STBIR_RESIZE * resize );
645//===============================================================
646
647
648// And this is the main function to perform the resize synchronously on one thread.
649STBIRDEF int stbir_resize_extended( STBIR_RESIZE * resize );
650
651
652//===============================================================
653// Use these functions for multithreading.
654// 1) You call stbir_build_samplers_with_splits first on the main thread
655// 2) Then stbir_resize_with_split on each thread
656// 3) stbir_free_samplers when done on the main thread
657//--------------------------------
658
659// This will build samplers for threading.
660// You can pass in the number of threads you'd like to use (try_splits).
661// It returns the number of splits (threads) that you can call it with.
662/// It might be less if the image resize can't be split up that many ways.
663
664STBIRDEF int stbir_build_samplers_with_splits( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, int try_splits );
665
666// This function does a split of the resizing (you call this fuction for each
667// split, on multiple threads). A split is a piece of the output resize pixel space.
668
669// Note that you MUST call stbir_build_samplers_with_splits before stbir_resize_extended_split!
670
671// Usually, you will always call stbir_resize_split with split_start as the thread_index
672// and "1" for the split_count.
673// But, if you have a weird situation where you MIGHT want 8 threads, but sometimes
674// only 4 threads, you can use 0,2,4,6 for the split_start's and use "2" for the
675// split_count each time to turn in into a 4 thread resize. (This is unusual).
676
677STBIRDEF int stbir_resize_extended_split( STBIR_RESIZE * resize, int split_start, int split_count );
678//===============================================================
679
680
681//===============================================================
682// Pixel Callbacks info:
683//--------------------------------
684
685// The input callback is super flexible - it calls you with the input address
686// (based on the stride and base pointer), it gives you an optional_output
687// pointer that you can fill, or you can just return your own pointer into
688// your own data.
689//
690// You can also do conversion from non-supported data types if necessary - in
691// this case, you ignore the input_ptr and just use the x and y parameters to
692// calculate your own input_ptr based on the size of each non-supported pixel.
693// (Something like the third example below.)
694//
695// You can also install just an input or just an output callback by setting the
696// callback that you don't want to zero.
697//
698// First example, progress: (getting a callback that you can monitor the progress):
699// void const * my_callback( void * optional_output, void const * input_ptr, int num_pixels, int x, int y, void * context )
700// {
701// percentage_done = y / input_height;
702// return input_ptr; // use buffer from call
703// }
704//
705// Next example, copying: (copy from some other buffer or stream):
706// void const * my_callback( void * optional_output, void const * input_ptr, int num_pixels, int x, int y, void * context )
707// {
708// CopyOrStreamData( optional_output, other_data_src, num_pixels * pixel_width_in_bytes );
709// return optional_output; // return the optional buffer that we filled
710// }
711//
712// Third example, input another buffer without copying: (zero-copy from other buffer):
713// void const * my_callback( void * optional_output, void const * input_ptr, int num_pixels, int x, int y, void * context )
714// {
715// void * pixels = ( (char*) other_image_base ) + ( y * other_image_stride ) + ( x * other_pixel_width_in_bytes );
716// return pixels; // return pointer to your data without copying
717// }
718//
719//
720// The output callback is considerably simpler - it just calls you so that you can dump
721// out each scanline. You could even directly copy out to disk if you have a simple format
722// like TGA or BMP. You can also convert to other output types here if you want.
723//
724// Simple example:
725// void const * my_output( void * output_ptr, int num_pixels, int y, void * context )
726// {
727// percentage_done = y / output_height;
728// fwrite( output_ptr, pixel_width_in_bytes, num_pixels, output_file );
729// }
730//===============================================================

1062 break; \

1126static stbir__inline stbir_uint8 stbir__linear_to_srgb_uchar(float in)
1127{
1128 static const stbir__FP32 almostone = { 0x3f7fffff }; // 1-eps
1129 static const stbir__FP32 minval = { (127-13) << 23 };
1130 stbir_uint32 tab,bias,scale,t;
1131 stbir__FP32 f;
1132
1133 // Clamp to [2^(-13), 1-eps]; these two values map to 0 and 1, respectively.
1134 // The tests are carefully written so that NaNs map to 0, same as in the reference
1135 // implementation.
1136 if (!(in > minval.f)) // written this way to catch NaNs
1137 return 0;
1138 if (in > almostone.f)
1139 return 255;
1140
1141 // Do the table lookup and unpack bias, scale
1142 f.f = in;
1143 tab = fp32_to_srgb8_tab4[(f.u - minval.u) >> 20];
1144 bias = (tab >> 16) << 9;
1145 scale = tab & 0xffff;
1146
1147 // Grab next-highest mantissa bits and perform linear interpolation
1148 t = (f.u >> 12) & 0xff;
1149 return (unsigned char) ((bias + scale*t) >> 16);
1150}

1422 stbir__simdf_load( o1, (ptr)+4 ); \

1425 { \

1428 tmp2 = _mm_unpacklo_ps(o2, o3); \

1431 o0 = _mm_movelh_ps(tmp0, tmp2); \
1432 o1 = _mm_movehl_ps(tmp2, tmp0); \
1433 o2 = _mm_movelh_ps(tmp1, tmp3); \
1434 o3 = _mm_movehl_ps(tmp3, tmp1); \
1435 }

2082 { \

2085 v128_t tmp = wasm_u8x16_narrow_i16x8(tmp0, tmp1); \

2090 #define stbir__simdf_load4_transposed( o0, o1, o2, o3, ptr ) \
2091 { \
2092 v128_t t0 = wasm_v128_load( ptr ); \
2093 v128_t t1 = wasm_v128_load( ptr+4 ); \
2094 v128_t t2 = wasm_v128_load( ptr+8 ); \
2095 v128_t t3 = wasm_v128_load( ptr+12 ); \
2096 v128_t s0 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(t0, t1, 0, 4, 2, 6); \
2097 v128_t s1 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(t0, t1, 1, 5, 3, 7); \
2098 v128_t s2 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(t2, t3, 0, 4, 2, 6); \
2099 v128_t s3 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(t2, t3, 1, 5, 3, 7); \
2100 o0 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(s0, s2, 0, 1, 4, 5); \
2101 o1 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(s1, s3, 0, 1, 4, 5); \
2102 o2 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(s0, s2, 2, 3, 6, 7); \
2103 o3 = wasm_i32x4_shuffle(s1, s3, 2, 3, 6, 7); \
2104 }

2223 // Fabian's half float routines, see: https://gist.github.com/rygorous/2156668
2224
2225 static stbir__inline float stbir__half_to_float( stbir__FP16 h )
2226 {
2227 static const stbir__FP32 magic = { (254 - 15) << 23 };
2228 static const stbir__FP32 was_infnan = { (127 + 16) << 23 };
2229 stbir__FP32 o;
2230
2231 o.u = (h.u & 0x7fff) << 13; // exponent/mantissa bits
2232 o.f *= magic.f; // exponent adjust
2233 if (o.f >= was_infnan.f) // make sure Inf/NaN survive
2234 o.u |= 255 << 23;
2235 o.u |= (h.u & 0x8000) << 16; // sign bit
2236 return o.f;
2237 }
2238
2239 static stbir__inline stbir__FP16 stbir__float_to_half(float val)
2240 {
2241 stbir__FP32 f32infty = { 255 << 23 };
2242 stbir__FP32 f16max = { (127 + 16) << 23 };
2243 stbir__FP32 denorm_magic = { ((127 - 15) + (23 - 10) + 1) << 23 };
2244 unsigned int sign_mask = 0x80000000u;
2245 stbir__FP16 o = { 0 };
2246 stbir__FP32 f;
2247 unsigned int sign;
2248
2249 f.f = val;
2250 sign = f.u & sign_mask;
2251 f.u ^= sign;
2252
2253 if (f.u >= f16max.u) // result is Inf or NaN (all exponent bits set)
2254 o.u = (f.u > f32infty.u) ? 0x7e00 : 0x7c00; // NaN->qNaN and Inf->Inf
2255 else // (De)normalized number or zero
2256 {
2257 if (f.u < (113 << 23)) // resulting FP16 is subnormal or zero
2258 {
2259 // use a magic value to align our 10 mantissa bits at the bottom of
2260 // the float. as long as FP addition is round-to-nearest-even this
2261 // just works.
2262 f.f += denorm_magic.f;
2263 // and one integer subtract of the bias later, we have our final float!
2264 o.u = (unsigned short) ( f.u - denorm_magic.u );
2265 }
2266 else
2267 {
2268 unsigned int mant_odd = (f.u >> 13) & 1; // resulting mantissa is odd
2269 // update exponent, rounding bias part 1
2270 f.u = f.u + ((15u - 127) << 23) + 0xfff;
2271 // rounding bias part 2
2272 f.u += mant_odd;
2273 // take the bits!
2274 o.u = (unsigned short) ( f.u >> 13 );
2275 }
2276 }
2277
2278 o.u |= sign >> 16;
2279 return o;
2280 }

2313 // Fabian's half float routines, see: https://gist.github.com/rygorous/2156668
2314 stbir__inline static void stbir__half_to_float_SIMD(float * output, void const * input)
2315 {
2316 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(mask_nosign, 0x7fff);
2317 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(smallest_normal, 0x0400);
2318 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(infinity, 0x7c00);
2319 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(expadjust_normal, (127 - 15) << 23);
2320 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(magic_denorm, 113 << 23);
2321
2322 __m128i i = _mm_loadu_si128 ( (__m128i const*)(input) );
2323 __m128i h = _mm_unpacklo_epi16 ( i, _mm_setzero_si128() );
2324 __m128i mnosign = STBIR__CONSTI(mask_nosign);
2325 __m128i eadjust = STBIR__CONSTI(expadjust_normal);
2326 __m128i smallest = STBIR__CONSTI(smallest_normal);
2327 __m128i infty = STBIR__CONSTI(infinity);
2328 __m128i expmant = _mm_and_si128(mnosign, h);
2329 __m128i justsign = _mm_xor_si128(h, expmant);
2330 __m128i b_notinfnan = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(infty, expmant);
2331 __m128i b_isdenorm = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(smallest, expmant);
2332 __m128i shifted = _mm_slli_epi32(expmant, 13);
2333 __m128i adj_infnan = _mm_andnot_si128(b_notinfnan, eadjust);
2334 __m128i adjusted = _mm_add_epi32(eadjust, shifted);
2335 __m128i den1 = _mm_add_epi32(shifted, STBIR__CONSTI(magic_denorm));
2336 __m128i adjusted2 = _mm_add_epi32(adjusted, adj_infnan);
2337 __m128 den2 = _mm_sub_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(den1), *(const __m128 *)&magic_denorm);
2338 __m128 adjusted3 = _mm_and_ps(den2, _mm_castsi128_ps(b_isdenorm));
2339 __m128 adjusted4 = _mm_andnot_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(b_isdenorm), _mm_castsi128_ps(adjusted2));
2340 __m128 adjusted5 = _mm_or_ps(adjusted3, adjusted4);
2341 __m128i sign = _mm_slli_epi32(justsign, 16);
2342 __m128 final = _mm_or_ps(adjusted5, _mm_castsi128_ps(sign));
2343 stbir__simdf_store( output + 0, final );
2344
2345 h = _mm_unpackhi_epi16 ( i, _mm_setzero_si128() );
2346 expmant = _mm_and_si128(mnosign, h);
2347 justsign = _mm_xor_si128(h, expmant);
2348 b_notinfnan = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(infty, expmant);
2349 b_isdenorm = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(smallest, expmant);
2350 shifted = _mm_slli_epi32(expmant, 13);
2351 adj_infnan = _mm_andnot_si128(b_notinfnan, eadjust);
2352 adjusted = _mm_add_epi32(eadjust, shifted);
2353 den1 = _mm_add_epi32(shifted, STBIR__CONSTI(magic_denorm));
2354 adjusted2 = _mm_add_epi32(adjusted, adj_infnan);
2355 den2 = _mm_sub_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(den1), *(const __m128 *)&magic_denorm);
2356 adjusted3 = _mm_and_ps(den2, _mm_castsi128_ps(b_isdenorm));
2357 adjusted4 = _mm_andnot_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(b_isdenorm), _mm_castsi128_ps(adjusted2));
2358 adjusted5 = _mm_or_ps(adjusted3, adjusted4);
2359 sign = _mm_slli_epi32(justsign, 16);
2360 final = _mm_or_ps(adjusted5, _mm_castsi128_ps(sign));
2361 stbir__simdf_store( output + 4, final );
2362
2363 // ~38 SSE2 ops for 8 values
2364 }
2365
2366 // Fabian's round-to-nearest-even float to half
2367 // ~48 SSE2 ops for 8 output
2368 stbir__inline static void stbir__float_to_half_SIMD(void * output, float const * input)
2369 {
2370 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(mask_sign, 0x80000000u);
2371 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(c_f16max, (127 + 16) << 23); // all FP32 values >=this round to +inf
2372 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(c_nanbit, 0x200);
2373 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(c_infty_as_fp16, 0x7c00);
2374 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(c_min_normal, (127 - 14) << 23); // smallest FP32 that yields a normalized FP16
2375 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(c_subnorm_magic, ((127 - 15) + (23 - 10) + 1) << 23);
2376 static const STBIR__SIMDI_CONST(c_normal_bias, 0xfff - ((127 - 15) << 23)); // adjust exponent and add mantissa rounding
2377
2378 __m128 f = _mm_loadu_ps(input);
2379 __m128 msign = _mm_castsi128_ps(STBIR__CONSTI(mask_sign));
2380 __m128 justsign = _mm_and_ps(msign, f);
2381 __m128 absf = _mm_xor_ps(f, justsign);
2382 __m128i absf_int = _mm_castps_si128(absf); // the cast is "free" (extra bypass latency, but no thruput hit)
2383 __m128i f16max = STBIR__CONSTI(c_f16max);
2384 __m128 b_isnan = _mm_cmpunord_ps(absf, absf); // is this a NaN?
2385 __m128i b_isregular = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(f16max, absf_int); // (sub)normalized or special?
2386 __m128i nanbit = _mm_and_si128(_mm_castps_si128(b_isnan), STBIR__CONSTI(c_nanbit));
2387 __m128i inf_or_nan = _mm_or_si128(nanbit, STBIR__CONSTI(c_infty_as_fp16)); // output for specials
2388
2389 __m128i min_normal = STBIR__CONSTI(c_min_normal);
2390 __m128i b_issub = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(min_normal, absf_int);
2391
2392 // "result is subnormal" path
2393 __m128 subnorm1 = _mm_add_ps(absf, _mm_castsi128_ps(STBIR__CONSTI(c_subnorm_magic))); // magic value to round output mantissa
2394 __m128i subnorm2 = _mm_sub_epi32(_mm_castps_si128(subnorm1), STBIR__CONSTI(c_subnorm_magic)); // subtract out bias
2395
2396 // "result is normal" path
2397 __m128i mantoddbit = _mm_slli_epi32(absf_int, 31 - 13); // shift bit 13 (mantissa LSB) to sign
2398 __m128i mantodd = _mm_srai_epi32(mantoddbit, 31); // -1 if FP16 mantissa odd, else 0
2399
2400 __m128i round1 = _mm_add_epi32(absf_int, STBIR__CONSTI(c_normal_bias));
2401 __m128i round2 = _mm_sub_epi32(round1, mantodd); // if mantissa LSB odd, bias towards rounding up (RTNE)
2402 __m128i normal = _mm_srli_epi32(round2, 13); // rounded result
2403
2404 // combine the two non-specials
2405 __m128i nonspecial = _mm_or_si128(_mm_and_si128(subnorm2, b_issub), _mm_andnot_si128(b_issub, normal));
2406
2407 // merge in specials as well
2408 __m128i joined = _mm_or_si128(_mm_and_si128(nonspecial, b_isregular), _mm_andnot_si128(b_isregular, inf_or_nan));
2409
2410 __m128i sign_shift = _mm_srai_epi32(_mm_castps_si128(justsign), 16);
2411 __m128i final2, final= _mm_or_si128(joined, sign_shift);
2412
2413 f = _mm_loadu_ps(input+4);
2414 justsign = _mm_and_ps(msign, f);
2415 absf = _mm_xor_ps(f, justsign);
2416 absf_int = _mm_castps_si128(absf); // the cast is "free" (extra bypass latency, but no thruput hit)
2417 b_isnan = _mm_cmpunord_ps(absf, absf); // is this a NaN?
2418 b_isregular = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(f16max, absf_int); // (sub)normalized or special?
2419 nanbit = _mm_and_si128(_mm_castps_si128(b_isnan), c_nanbit);
2420 inf_or_nan = _mm_or_si128(nanbit, STBIR__CONSTI(c_infty_as_fp16)); // output for specials
2421
2422 b_issub = _mm_cmpgt_epi32(min_normal, absf_int);
2423
2424 // "result is subnormal" path
2425 subnorm1 = _mm_add_ps(absf, _mm_castsi128_ps(STBIR__CONSTI(c_subnorm_magic))); // magic value to round output mantissa
2426 subnorm2 = _mm_sub_epi32(_mm_castps_si128(subnorm1), STBIR__CONSTI(c_subnorm_magic)); // subtract out bias
2427
2428 // "result is normal" path
2429 mantoddbit = _mm_slli_epi32(absf_int, 31 - 13); // shift bit 13 (mantissa LSB) to sign
2430 mantodd = _mm_srai_epi32(mantoddbit, 31); // -1 if FP16 mantissa odd, else 0
2431
2432 round1 = _mm_add_epi32(absf_int, STBIR__CONSTI(c_normal_bias));
2433 round2 = _mm_sub_epi32(round1, mantodd); // if mantissa LSB odd, bias towards rounding up (RTNE)
2434 normal = _mm_srli_epi32(round2, 13); // rounded result
2435
2436 // combine the two non-specials
2437 nonspecial = _mm_or_si128(_mm_and_si128(subnorm2, b_issub), _mm_andnot_si128(b_issub, normal));
2438
2439 // merge in specials as well
2440 joined = _mm_or_si128(_mm_and_si128(nonspecial, b_isregular), _mm_andnot_si128(b_isregular, inf_or_nan));
2441
2442 sign_shift = _mm_srai_epi32(_mm_castps_si128(justsign), 16);
2443 final2 = _mm_or_si128(joined, sign_shift);
2444 final = _mm_packs_epi32(final, final2);
2445 stbir__simdi_store( output,final );
2446 }

2566// Basically, in simd mode, we unroll the proper amount, and we don't want
2567// the non-simd remnant loops to be unroll because they only run a few times
2568// Adding this switch saves about 5K on clang which is Captain Unroll the 3rd.
2569#define STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR( star ) STBIR_STREAMOUT_PTR( star )
2570#define STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL(ptr) STBIR_NO_UNROLL(ptr)
2571#define STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START STBIR_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START
2572#define STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START_INF_FOR STBIR_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START_INF_FOR
2573
2574#ifdef STBIR_MEMCPY
2575#undef STBIR_MEMCPY
2576#endif
2577#define STBIR_MEMCPY stbir_simd_memcpy
2578
2579// override normal use of memcpy with much simpler copy (faster and smaller with our sized copies)
2580static void stbir_simd_memcpy( void * dest, void const * src, size_t bytes )
2581{
2582 char STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR (*) d = (char*) dest;
2583 char STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR( * ) d_end = ((char*) dest) + bytes;
2584 ptrdiff_t ofs_to_src = (char*)src - (char*)dest;
2585
2586 // check overlaps
2587 STBIR_ASSERT( ( ( d >= ( (char*)src) + bytes ) ) || ( ( d + bytes ) <= (char*)src ) );
2588
2589 if ( bytes < (16*stbir__simdfX_float_count) )
2590 {
2591 if ( bytes < 16 )
2592 {
2593 if ( bytes )
2594 {
2595 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START
2596 do
2597 {
2598 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL(d);
2599 d[ 0 ] = d[ ofs_to_src ];
2600 ++d;
2601 } while ( d < d_end );
2602 }
2603 }
2604 else
2605 {
2606 stbir__simdf x;
2607 // do one unaligned to get us aligned for the stream out below
2608 stbir__simdf_load( x, ( d + ofs_to_src ) );
2609 stbir__simdf_store( d, x );
2610 d = (char*)( ( ( (size_t)d ) + 16 ) & ~15 );
2611
2612 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START_INF_FOR
2613 for(;;)
2614 {
2615 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL(d);
2616
2617 if ( d > ( d_end - 16 ) )
2618 {
2619 if ( d == d_end )
2620 return;
2621 d = d_end - 16;
2622 }
2623
2624 stbir__simdf_load( x, ( d + ofs_to_src ) );
2625 stbir__simdf_store( d, x );
2626 d += 16;
2627 }
2628 }
2629 }
2630 else
2631 {
2632 stbir__simdfX x0,x1,x2,x3;
2633
2634 // do one unaligned to get us aligned for the stream out below
2635 stbir__simdfX_load( x0, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 0*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2636 stbir__simdfX_load( x1, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 4*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2637 stbir__simdfX_load( x2, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 8*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2638 stbir__simdfX_load( x3, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 12*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2639 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 0*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x0 );
2640 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 4*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x1 );
2641 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 8*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x2 );
2642 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 12*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x3 );
2643 d = (char*)( ( ( (size_t)d ) + (16*stbir__simdfX_float_count) ) & ~((16*stbir__simdfX_float_count)-1) );
2644
2645 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START_INF_FOR
2646 for(;;)
2647 {
2648 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL(d);
2649
2650 if ( d > ( d_end - (16*stbir__simdfX_float_count) ) )
2651 {
2652 if ( d == d_end )
2653 return;
2654 d = d_end - (16*stbir__simdfX_float_count);
2655 }
2656
2657 stbir__simdfX_load( x0, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 0*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2658 stbir__simdfX_load( x1, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 4*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2659 stbir__simdfX_load( x2, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 8*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2660 stbir__simdfX_load( x3, ( d + ofs_to_src ) + 12*stbir__simdfX_float_count );
2661 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 0*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x0 );
2662 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 4*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x1 );
2663 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 8*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x2 );
2664 stbir__simdfX_store( d + 12*stbir__simdfX_float_count, x3 );
2665 d += (16*stbir__simdfX_float_count);
2666 }
2667 }
2668}

2670// memcpy that is specically intentionally overlapping (src is smaller then dest, so can be
2671// a normal forward copy, bytes is divisible by 4 and bytes is greater than or equal to
2672// the diff between dest and src)
2673static void stbir_overlapping_memcpy( void * dest, void const * src, size_t bytes )
2674{
2675 char STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR (*) sd = (char*) src;
2676 char STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR( * ) s_end = ((char*) src) + bytes;
2677 ptrdiff_t ofs_to_dest = (char*)dest - (char*)src;
2678
2679 if ( ofs_to_dest >= 16 ) // is the overlap more than 16 away?
2680 {
2681 char STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR( * ) s_end16 = ((char*) src) + (bytes&~15);
2682 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START
2683 do
2684 {
2685 stbir__simdf x;
2686 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL(sd);
2687 stbir__simdf_load( x, sd );
2688 stbir__simdf_store( ( sd + ofs_to_dest ), x );
2689 sd += 16;
2690 } while ( sd < s_end16 );
2691
2692 if ( sd == s_end )
2693 return;
2694 }
2695
2696 do
2697 {
2698 STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL(sd);
2699 *(int*)( sd + ofs_to_dest ) = *(int*) sd;
2700 sd += 4;
2701 } while ( sd < s_end );
2702}

2707#define STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR( star ) STBIR_STREAMOUT_PTR( star )
2708#define STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL(ptr)
2709#define STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START
2710#define STBIR_SIMD_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START_INF_FOR
2711
2712#endif // SSE2

2828static void stbir_overlapping_memcpy( void * dest, void const * src, size_t bytes )

2830 char STBIR_SIMD_STREAMOUT_PTR (*) sd = (char*) src;

2849 STBIR_NO_UNROLL_LOOP_START

2860static float stbir__filter_trapezoid(float x, float scale, void * user_data)
2861{
2862 float halfscale = scale / 2;
2863 float t = 0.5f + halfscale;
2864 STBIR_ASSERT(scale <= 1);
2865 STBIR__UNUSED(user_data);
2866
2867 if ( x < 0.0f ) x = -x;
2868
2869 if (x >= t)
2870 return 0.0f;
2871 else
2872 {
2873 float r = 0.5f - halfscale;
2874 if (x <= r)
2875 return 1.0f;
2876 else
2877 return (t - x) / scale;
2878 }
2879}
2880
2881static float stbir__support_trapezoid(float scale, void * user_data)
2882{
2883 STBIR__UNUSED(user_data);
2884 return 0.5f + scale / 2.0f;
2885}

2887static float stbir__filter_triangle(float x, float s, void * user_data)
2888{
2889 STBIR__UNUSED(s);
2890 STBIR__UNUSED(user_data);
2891
2892 if ( x < 0.0f ) x = -x;
2893
2894 if (x <= 1.0f)
2895 return 1.0f - x;
2896 else
2897 return 0.0f;
2898}

2900static float stbir__filter_point(float x, float s, void * user_data)
2901{
2902 STBIR__UNUSED(x);
2903 STBIR__UNUSED(s);
2904 STBIR__UNUSED(user_data);
2905
2906 return 1.0f;

2909static float stbir__filter_cubic(float x, float s, void * user_data)
2910{
2911 STBIR__UNUSED(s);
2912 STBIR__UNUSED(user_data);
2913
2914 if ( x < 0.0f ) x = -x;
2915
2916 if (x < 1.0f)
2917 return (4.0f + x*x*(3.0f*x - 6.0f))/6.0f;
2918 else if (x < 2.0f)
2919 return (8.0f + x*(-12.0f + x*(6.0f - x)))/6.0f;
2920
2921 return (0.0f);
2922}
2923
2924static float stbir__filter_catmullrom(float x, float s, void * user_data)
2925{
2926 STBIR__UNUSED(s);
2927 STBIR__UNUSED(user_data);
2928
2929 if ( x < 0.0f ) x = -x;
2930
2931 if (x < 1.0f)
2932 return 1.0f - x*x*(2.5f - 1.5f*x);
2933 else if (x < 2.0f)
2934 return 2.0f - x*(4.0f + x*(0.5f*x - 2.5f));
2935
2936 return (0.0f);
2937}
2938
2939static float stbir__filter_mitchell(float x, float s, void * user_data)
2940{
2941 STBIR__UNUSED(s);
2942 STBIR__UNUSED(user_data);
2943
2944 if ( x < 0.0f ) x = -x;
2945
2946 if (x < 1.0f)
2947 return (16.0f + x*x*(21.0f * x - 36.0f))/18.0f;
2948 else if (x < 2.0f)
2949 return (32.0f + x*(-60.0f + x*(36.0f - 7.0f*x)))/18.0f;
2950
2951 return (0.0f);
2952}

2975// This is the maximum number of input samples that can affect an output sample
2976// with the given filter from the output pixel's perspective
2977static int stbir__get_filter_pixel_width(stbir__support_callback * support, float scale, void * user_data)
2978{
2979 STBIR_ASSERT(support != 0);
2980
2981 if ( scale >= ( 1.0f-stbir__small_float ) ) // upscale
2982 return (int)STBIR_CEILF(support(1.0f/scale,user_data) * 2.0f);
2983 else
2984 return (int)STBIR_CEILF(support(scale,user_data) * 2.0f / scale);
2985}
2986
2987// this is how many coefficents per run of the filter (which is different
2988// from the filter_pixel_width depending on if we are scattering or gathering)
2989static int stbir__get_coefficient_width(stbir__sampler * samp, int is_gather, void * user_data)
2990{
2991 float scale = samp->scale_info.scale;
2992 stbir__support_callback * support = samp->filter_support;
2993
2994 switch( is_gather )
2995 {
2996 case 1:
2997 return (int)STBIR_CEILF(support(1.0f / scale, user_data) * 2.0f);
2998 case 2:
2999 return (int)STBIR_CEILF(support(scale, user_data) * 2.0f / scale);
3000 case 0:
3001 return (int)STBIR_CEILF(support(scale, user_data) * 2.0f);
3002 default:
3003 STBIR_ASSERT( (is_gather >= 0 ) && (is_gather <= 2 ) );
3004 return 0;
3005 }
3006}

3012 else
3013 return (samp->scale_info.input_full_size + samp->filter_pixel_margin * 2);

3016static int stbir__edge_zero_full( int n, int max )
3017{
3018 STBIR__UNUSED(n);
3019 STBIR__UNUSED(max);
3020 return 0; // NOTREACHED
3021}
3022
3023static int stbir__edge_clamp_full( int n, int max )
3024{
3025 if (n < 0)
3026 return 0;
3027
3028 if (n >= max)
3029 return max - 1;
3030
3031 return n; // NOTREACHED
3032}
3033
3034static int stbir__edge_reflect_full( int n, int max )
3035{
3036 if (n < 0)
3037 {
3038 if (n > -max)
3039 return -n;
3040 else
3041 return max - 1;
3042 }
3043
3044 if (n >= max)
3045 {
3046 int max2 = max * 2;
3047 if (n >= max2)
3048 return 0;
3049 else
3050 return max2 - n - 1;
3051 }
3052
3053 return n; // NOTREACHED
3054}
3055
3056static int stbir__edge_wrap_full( int n, int max )
3057{
3058 if (n >= 0)
3059 return (n % max);
3060 else
3061 {
3062 int m = (-n) % max;
3063
3064 if (m != 0)
3065 m = max - m;
3066
3067 return (m);
3068 }
3069}
3070
3071typedef int stbir__edge_wrap_func( int n, int max );
3072static stbir__edge_wrap_func * stbir__edge_wrap_slow[] =
3073{
3074 stbir__edge_clamp_full, // STBIR_EDGE_CLAMP
3075 stbir__edge_reflect_full, // STBIR_EDGE_REFLECT
3076 stbir__edge_wrap_full, // STBIR_EDGE_WRAP
3077 stbir__edge_zero_full, // STBIR_EDGE_ZERO
3078};

3081{
